$Comment: Icon intentionally omitted: StationService#blockItemIdAt already falls back to the anchor block's own BlockType id at engage time when Identity.Icon is absent/blank, and this jar's own default Sawmill block shares the same id (RPG_Station_Sawmill, filename = item id) - so the summary-HUD crest already shows the station's own block icon with zero duplicated id to drift, the same reasoning the pack's own Sawmill.json/Anvil.json use. Loot.Lootables is the unified LootRef group (asset.LootRef); Recipe here authors only FromCrafting, never Conversions. FromCrafting.Categories includes 'WoodPlanks', 'DecorativePlanks', and 'OrnatePlanks' - genuine native categories (every Wood_<Species>_{Planks,Decorative,Ornate}.json shares the same Wood_<Species>_Trunk ResourceTypeId input and the same 'Builders'/StructuralCrafting bench, only the recipe Category differs), so this is native-recipe composition, not invented content. The deriver surfaces 3 output categories per log species (33 total conversions); StationRecipeDeriver stamps each derived Conversion with its source category so the sneak+F picker can offer 'Planks'/'Decorative'/'Ornate' as the three choices for whatever log the player is holding - a single-log input, multiple valid outputs, exactly the picker's reason to exist. Recipe.Yield is the sawmill's yield edge over hand-crafting, resolved fresh every cycle off the tool actually being held. Base 1 matches the native yield (every derived recipe in all three categories authors OutputQuantity 1 against a single-trunk Input, true across all 11 wood species - e.g. Wood_Hardwood_Planks / Wood_Hardwood_Decorative / Wood_Hardwood_Ornate), and the Bonus ladder is what pays for the milling time, so a starter hatchet earns nothing extra and every upgrade is felt. Values sum THREE tool axes because no two of them can rank the vanilla hatchet ladder alone: quality (the native ItemQuality.QualityValue - Junk 0, Common 1, Uncommon 2, Rare 3, Epic 4, Legendary 5) at weight 10.0 dominates, item level at 0.1 breaks ties inside a quality tier, and gather power at 1.0 rewards the genuinely better cutter. Quality alone cannot separate Wood/Crude from Copper (all three are Common) and power alone cannot either (Wood and Copper share an identical 0.2 Woods power, and power SATURATES at 0.5 from the mid ladder up, flattening every top tier); item level separates them (4/4 vs 11) but must stay a small term, because it does not track rarity - Onyxium is Epic at item level 4, so a level-led formula would rank it below a copper hatchet. The resulting curve over the vanilla hatchets: Wood 10.6 and Crude 10.55 reach no floor -> 1 plank; Copper 11.3 -> 2; Iron 22.3 -> 2.5; Thorium 33.5, Cobalt 34.0, Adamantite 34.5 -> 3; Onyxium 40.9 and Mithril 45.5 -> 4. Iron's fractional 2.5 is real, not rounded: a fractional yield pays its whole part every cycle and rolls only the remainder, so Iron gives 2 planks plus a third half the time and averages exactly 2.5. Every number here is a tunable leaf - reweight the Values to change what the curve rewards, move a floor Min to change which tier earns which step, or append a floor for a modded tier above Epic (floors are NOT cumulative, the highest one reached wins). Scale/Min/Max compose on top if wanted. A station deriving categories whose native recipes are NOT 1:1 should author Scale rather than Base, since the native quantity is not readable at the derivation seam. A plain-F press with no picker selection defaults to the first authored FromCrafting.Categories entry - so the array order below (WoodPlanks first) is the default priority (the deriver's alphabetical output-id sort would otherwise make Decorative the first runnable). Reorder Categories to change the plain-F default; sneak+F still offers all three. This is resolved engine-side at the effective-category point (StationService#effectiveCategory), not the deriver sort, so the balance-neutral claim above stays true. The Puppet group, Custody.Display, and Work.CycleMs 4805 below are this jar's own shipped standalone defaults, tuned in-game so the standalone sawmill looks right with no pack installed: Puppet.Offset.Z 1.0 and Yaw 0.0 position the working puppet at the bench; Custody.Display.Offset.Y -0.1 embeds the placed log slightly into the bench top; Work.CycleMs 4805 is the tuned cadence. ExtensionAsset carries real Puppet/Custody keys with per-leaf overlay semantics, so a pack re-skinning this station authors only the leaves it re-tunes and inherits the rest of these defaults - see asset/ExtensionAsset.java rule 5 and station/ExtensionCatalog.java's overlayPuppet/overlayCustody. Work declares no PerCycleContributions: this jar's content is progression-free by design, and a pack layers its own on through an ExtensionAsset. Tool.PowerScale is deliberately KEPT even with nothing to scale - the tool ladder is pre-wired and tuned, so a pack that appends contributions inherits a working power curve for free rather than re-deriving one.
